items.title: Adopted finite-regulator polynomial model
items.design_state: Complete adopted finite-regulator data and scope. The assigned C01 unit-definition supplier has no Step 1 readiness record, so this item is escalated; the QFT-IR01 polynomial definition is current-ready.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) as in
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]]; it supplies the stated
Hilbert-space construction and is not a physical measurement assumption. Fix
one finite nonempty label set $J$ with $N:=|J|\ge1$, an enumeration of $J$ by
$\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and dimensionless real coordinates
$q=(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\in\mathbb R^N$. Each label indexes one coordinate; no
spatial geometry or limit in $N$ is part of these data. The coordinate space,
Hilbert space, and polynomial differential expression are those of
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]]:
$H_N=L^2(\mathbb R^N,dq;\mathbb C)$, with inner product linear in its first
variable, $D_0=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb C)$, and

$$h_0u=-\sum_{j=1}^N a_j\partial_j^2u+V(q)u,\qquad u\in D_0,$$

where $a_j>0$ and $V$ is a real polynomial. Require fixed constants $c>0$ and
$C_0\ge0$ such that

$$V(q)\ge c|q|^2-C_0\qquad(q\in\mathbb R^N).$$

For $j=1,\ldots,N$ define dimensionless linear maps
$Q_j,P_j:D_0\to D_0$ by
$$Q_ju(q):=q_ju(q),\qquad P_ju(q):=-i\partial_ju(q).$$
For maps preserving $D_0$, write $[A,B]u:=A(Bu)-B(Au)$. For every
$u\in D_0$ these maps obey
$$[Q_i,Q_j]u=0,\qquad [P_i,P_j]u=0,\qquad [Q_i,P_j]u=i\delta_{ij}u,$$
where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise. In this finite-coordinate
model, the mixed identity follows from
$-iq_i\partial_j u+i\partial_j(q_i u)=i\delta_{ij}u$; the other two vanish
by commutativity of coordinate multiplication and mixed derivatives. A
**bosonic mode** means one such
coordinate-momentum pair with these commutation relations on $D_0$; this names
the algebraic commutation convention and adds no state-space construction
beyond $H_N$. A **polynomial interaction term** means a
monomial of total degree at least three in $V$; the model is interacting in
this finite-coordinate sense exactly when at least one such term has nonzero
coefficient. This terminology asserts no continuum field interaction or
scattering construction.

Define $V(Q):D_0\to D_0$ by $(V(Q)u)(q):=V(q)u(q)$. Then
$$h_0u=\sum_{j=1}^N a_jP_j^2u+V(Q)u\qquad(u\in D_0).$$
All terms here are dimensionless, and the physical energy unit enters only
through the scale $E_*$ below.

For this physical model, take $q_j$, $a_j$, $c$, $C_0$, and the coefficients
of $V$ to be dimensionless. Adopt a positive energy scale $E_*$ in joules as
primitive finite-regulator data, and use $\hbar$ in joule-seconds under
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. When the mathematical supplier
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]] constructs its specified
self-adjoint form realization $h$ of $h_0$, the model Hamiltonian is
$H_{\rm phys}:=E_*h$ on that supplied domain. This postulate adopts the
finite-regulator polynomial data; it does not assert that the initial
differential expression is self-adjoint or choose an operator domain by
itself.

The finite label set and polynomial are held fixed. A finite spatial regulator
is not thereby Lorentz invariant, and this model asserts no continuum or
infinite-volume limit, no convergence of a perturbation series, and no
reported observation. Its parameters are selected model inputs, not measured
values.

items.title: Finite-regulator temperature and inverse-energy parameter
items.design_state: Complete local temperature and inverse-energy definition. Its framework-units supplier lacks a Step 1 readiness record, and its model postulate is escalated; this item is escalated.
items.statement:
For the fixed model of [[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]], use the SI
energy-unit convention of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. A declared temperature
input is a scalar $T>0$ with unit kelvin (K). Use the SI-defining Boltzmann
constant
$$k_B:=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}.$$
This exact value is the one stated by the BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition,
version 4.01, §§2.2 and 2.3.1. Define the physical inverse-energy parameter

$$\beta_{\rm phys}:=\frac{1}{k_BT}\quad[\mathrm{J^{-1}}],$$

and its dimensionless form

$$\widehat\beta:=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}.$$

The product $k_BT$ has unit joule, and $\widehat\beta$ is dimensionless
because $E_*$ has unit joule. Since $k_B>0$ and $T>0$, both inverse parameters
are defined and positive. The temperature $T$ is a declared model input; this
definition does not infer it from a state or an experiment. It defines a
parameter convention only and asserts no dynamical thermalization.

items.title: Constructed regulated polynomial-model evolution
items.design_state: Complete conditional proof and SI time conversion. The QFT-IR01 mathematical suppliers are current-ready, but the selected-model postulate and C01 constructed-model postulate lack Step 1 readiness records; this item is escalated.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use one fixed finite-regulator data set from
[[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]], and let $h$ be the self-adjoint form
realization supplied by
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]], with domain $D(h)$ and
eigenpairs $(\psi_n,\lambda_n)$. Let $E_*>0$ joules and set
$H_{\rm phys}:=E_*h$ on $D(h)$. For physical time $\tau$ in seconds define

$$U_{\rm phys}(\tau):=U(E_*\tau/\hbar),$$

where $U(s)$ is the dimensionless-parameter group of
[[thm-qft-regulated-global-unitary-evolution]]. Then $U_{\rm phys}$ is a
strongly continuous unitary group, $U_{\rm phys}(0)=I$,
$U_{\rm phys}(\tau_1+\tau_2)=U_{\rm phys}(\tau_1)U_{\rm phys}(\tau_2)$,
and $\|U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi\|=\|\psi\|$ for every $\psi\in H_N$.
Its norm derivative exists exactly for $\psi\in D(h)$, and then

$$\frac{d}{d\tau}U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{\rm phys}U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi.$$

The result is a conditional deduction for the selected finite-regulator
model. It is not an empirical observation or a continuum-limit theorem.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Under Countable Choice [A1], the hypotheses of [F1] hold, so $h$ is self-adjoint on $D(h)$. Multiplication by the positive real scalar $E_*$ preserves self-adjointness and the domain, so $H_{\rm phys}=E_*h$ is self-adjoint on $D(h)$ with eigenvalues $E_*\lambda_n$. The units in [A2] make $E_*\tau/\hbar$ dimensionless. [A1, A2, F1, algebra]

2.1 Put $s=E_*\tau/\hbar$. Since this is a real linear change of parameter, Countable Choice [A1] discharges the hypothesis of [F2], which gives unitarity, strong continuity, the identity at zero, and the group law for $U_{\rm phys}(\tau)=U(s)$. Unitarity also gives $\|U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi\|=\|\psi\|$. [A1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 If $\psi\in D(h)$, the chain rule and [F2] give $\frac{d}{d\tau}U(E_*\tau/\hbar)\psi =-i(E_*/\hbar)hU(E_*\tau/\hbar)\psi =-iH_{\rm phys}U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi/\hbar$. Conversely, because $E_*/\hbar>0$, the change $s=E_*\tau/\hbar$ is invertible, so norm differentiability in $\tau$ is equivalent to differentiability in $s$; [F2] makes its domain exactly $D(h)$. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [A3] supplies the physical reading of this already constructed self-adjoint Hamiltonian and group as the selected model's Schrödinger evolution. It adds no existence claim beyond [F1] and [F2], and no empirical premise is used. [A1, A3, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: Adopted finite-regulator equilibrium state
items.design_state: Complete adopted positive-temperature state assignment with the QFT-IR01 trace bound as its well-definedness input. The QFT-IR01 trace theorem is current-ready, but the local model postulate is escalated; this item is escalated.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the finite-regulator
spectral and trace construction. For the fixed model of
[[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]] and a declared
temperature input $T>0$, use
[[def-qft-regulated-thermal-parameter]] to set
$\beta_{\rm phys}=(k_BT)^{-1}$ and
$\widehat\beta=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}>0$. Let $h$ be the model's specified
self-adjoint form realization and $H_{\rm phys}=E_*h$. When the finite-mode
coercivity hypotheses hold, [[thm-qft-regulated-gibbs-trace]] proves that
$\rho_\gamma$ is positive trace class with finite positive trace for every
dimensionless $\gamma>0$. Make its spectral construction explicit: let
$(\psi_k,\lambda_k)_{k\ge0}$ be the complete orthonormal eigenbasis and
repeated eigenvalues used in that supplier. For $f\in H_N$, define

$$G_\gamma f:=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-\gamma\lambda_k}\langle f,\psi_k\rangle\psi_k.$$

The vector series converges in $H_N$ for every $f$, and this is the action of
the supplier's operator $\rho_\gamma$, obtained there as the operator-norm
limit of its finite-rank truncations. In this item the notation
$e^{-\gamma h}$ means this explicitly defined operator $G_\gamma$. Since
$H_{\rm phys}\psi_k=E_*\lambda_k\psi_k$, define
$e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}$ on $H_N$ by the corresponding series
$e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}f:=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}E_*\lambda_k}\langle f,\psi_k\rangle\psi_k$.
Since $\widehat\beta=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}$, its coefficients equal those of
$G_{\widehat\beta}$ term by term, and both series converge in $H_N$.
Therefore, as operators on $H_N$,
$e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}=G_{\widehat\beta}=e^{-\widehat\beta h}$.
The Gibbs-trace supplier consequently applies to exactly the operator in the
state assignment below. Adopt the normalized operator

$$\rho_T:=\frac{e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}}{Z_T}=\frac{e^{-\widehat\beta h}}{Z_T},\qquad Z_T:=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}})=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\widehat\beta h})$$

as this finite-regulator model's canonical equilibrium state. This is a
physical state assignment, not a deduction that the dynamics reach
equilibrium. It asserts no infinite-volume trace, no zero-temperature state,
and no empirical observation.

items.title: Finite-regulator Gibbs predictions
items.design_state: Complete conditional proof with physical inverse temperature rescaled by E_* before applying the finite mathematical trace theorem. The QFT-IR01 trace input is current-ready, but the local equilibrium-state postulate and C01 constructed-model postulate lack current readiness; this item is escalated.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the finite-regulator coercivity hypotheses of
[[thm-qft-regulated-gibbs-trace]]. Use the model state of
[[post-qft-regulated-equilibrium-state]] and the inverse-energy parameters of
[[def-qft-regulated-thermal-parameter]]. Let
$\alpha_j:=\sqrt{a_jc}$, $j=1,\ldots,N$, for the dimensionless kinetic
coefficients and coercivity constant in the model, and let
$C_0\ge0$ be its potential lower-bound shift. Then

$$0<Z_T=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}\le e^{\widehat\beta C_0}\prod_{j=1}^N\frac{e^{-\widehat\beta\alpha_j}}{1-e^{-2\widehat\beta\alpha_j}}<\infty,$$

where $\lambda_k$ are the eigenvalues of $h$. The adopted state
$\rho_T$ is a positive trace-class operator with trace one. For every
bounded linear operator $B:H_N\to H_N$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_TB)=Z_T^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}\langle B\psi_k,\psi_k\rangle,$$

and the series is absolutely convergent. If $E_a$ is an effect in a supplied
normalized finite instrument of
[[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]], this trace is its adopted
canonical model probability. These are conditional finite-regulator
predictions, not measured outcomes or a continuum-limit claim.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 By [F2], $\widehat\beta=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}>0$ is dimensionless. For each $f\in H_N$, the series defining $e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}f$ has coefficients $e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}E_*\lambda_k}\langle f,\psi_k\rangle$, while the series defining $e^{-\widehat\beta h}f$ has coefficients $e^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}\langle f,\psi_k\rangle$. These coefficients are equal term by term, and both series converge in $H_N$; hence $e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}=e^{-\widehat\beta h}=G_{\widehat\beta}$ as operators. The trace supplied by [F1] is therefore $Z_T=\sum_ke^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}$. [A2, F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 Under Countable Choice [A1], apply [F1] at $\widehat\beta>0$. It gives $Z_T>0$, the stated finite upper bound, and trace-class positivity of $G_{\widehat\beta}=e^{-\widehat\beta h}$. Dividing by $Z_T$ yields $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_T)=1$ and preserves positivity and trace class. [A1, A2, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Under the same Countable Choice assumption [A1], for bounded $B$, [F1]
gives the absolutely convergent sum for $\operatorname{Tr}(G_{\widehat\beta}B)$. Since $\rho_T=Z_T^{-1}G_{\widehat\beta}$, linearity of the trace and $Z_T>0$ give the displayed normalized formula. If $B=E_a$ is an effect in the instrument of [A3], that postulate supplies its physical model probability interpretation; the finite trace calculation supplies its value. [A1, A2, A3, F1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Controlled quartic-model ground-energy bound
items.design_state: Complete conditional form comparison and Gaussian trial-state proof. Its QFT-IR01 mathematical suppliers are current-ready, but the selected-model and C01 constructed-model postulates lack current Step 1 readiness records; this item is escalated.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use one fixed one-mode regulator of
[[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]] with
dimensionless $a>0$, $r>0$, and $\lambda\ge0$. Here $r$ is a polynomial
coefficient, not an SI rest mass. Take
$V_\lambda(q)=\frac{r^2}{2}q^2+\lambda q^4$ on
$H_1=L^2(\mathbb R,dq;\mathbb C)$, with the form realization from
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]]. Let $\epsilon_g(\lambda)$
be its least eigenvalue. The physical ground-energy prediction for the
adopted scale $E_*>0$ joules is
$E_g^{\rm phys}(\lambda):=E_*\epsilon_g(\lambda)$. Then

$$0\le E_g^{\rm phys}(\lambda)-E_g^{\rm phys}(0)\le \frac{3E_*a\lambda}{2r^2}.$$

For $\lambda>0$, the potential has a nonzero degree-four term and is
interacting in the finite-coordinate sense defined by
[[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]]. This conclusion makes no claim about
field scattering or a continuum field theory. The inequality is an exact fixed-regulator model
deduction; it supplies neither an observed energy nor a perturbation-series
or continuum-limit claim.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Since $V_\lambda(q)=r^2q^2/2+\lambda q^4\ge (r^2/2)q^2$, the coercivity hypotheses of [F1] and [F4] hold with $c=r^2/2$ and $C_0=0$. Countable Choice [A1] therefore gives the form domains of [F1] and the self-adjoint compact-resolvent form realizations with attained least eigenvalues from [F4], for both $q_\lambda$ and $q_0$. If $\lambda>0$, the term $\lambda q^4$ is an interaction term by the finite-coordinate definition in [A2]. [A1, A2, F1, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 On $C_c^\infty$, the shifted form norms obey $\|u\|_{Q_0}^2\le\|u\|_{Q_\lambda}^2$ because their difference is $\lambda\int q^4|u|^2dq\ge0$. Hence the identity extends continuously $Q_\lambda\to Q_0$, and the two continuous injections into $L^2$ identify the same representative. On the core, $q_\lambda(u)=q_0(u)+\lambda\int q^4|u|^2dq\ge q_0(u)$; approximating any $u\in Q_\lambda$ by core elements and using continuity of both forms passes this inequality to $u$. For a normalized $u$, [F3] gives $q_0(u)\ge\epsilon_g(0)$, so taking the infimum on $Q_\lambda$ yields $\epsilon_g(\lambda)\ge\epsilon_g(0)$. [A1, F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Let $g_b(q)=(b/\pi)^{1/4}e^{-bq^2/2}$ with $b=r/\sqrt{2a}$, the normalized ground function in [F2] for $c=r^2/2$. Choose the smooth cutoff $\chi_R(q)=\chi(q/R)$ from [F2], with $\chi=1$ on $[-1,1]$, $\chi=0$ outside $[-2,2]$, and $|\chi_R'|\le C/R$. Then $u_R=\chi_Rg_b\in C_c^\infty$. For $S>R$, $u_R-u_S$ is supported where $|q|\ge R$, and $\|(u_R-u_S)'\|_2\le\|1_{|q|\ge R}g_b'\|_2 +C(R^{-1}+S^{-1})\|1_{|q|\ge R}g_b\|_2\to0$. The weighted part of its $Q_\lambda$ norm is bounded in square by $\int_{|q|\ge R}(r^2q^2/2+\lambda q^4+2)|g_b(q)|^2dq\to0$. These tails vanish because each polynomial times $e^{-bq^2}$ is integrable: for large $|q|$, its product with $|q|^2$ is bounded. Thus $(u_R)$ is $Q_\lambda$-Cauchy. Its $L^2$ limit is $g_b$, so injectivity in [F1] gives $g_b\in Q_\lambda$. [A1, F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 From $g_b'=-bqg_b$ and $\|g_b\|_2=1$, integrate the derivatives of $q e^{-bq^2}$ and $q^3e^{-bq^2}$ over $\mathbb R$. Their boundary terms vanish by Gaussian decay, giving $\int q^2|g_b|^2dq=1/(2b)$ and $\int q^4|g_b|^2dq=3/(4b^2)$. Hence $q_\lambda(g_b)=ab/2+r^2/(4b)+3\lambda/(4b^2)$. At $b=r/\sqrt{2a}$, the first two terms equal $\epsilon_g(0)=r\sqrt{a/2}$ by [F2], and the last term is $3a\lambda/(2r^2)$. [A1, F2, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 Since $g_b\in Q_\lambda$ is normalized, [F3] gives $\epsilon_g(\lambda)\le q_\lambda(g_b)$. Combining this with step 2.1 and step 3.1 yields $0\le\epsilon_g(\lambda)-\epsilon_g(0)\le3a\lambda/(2r^2)$. [A1, F3, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Multiplication by $E_*>0$ preserves both inequalities and gives the stated joule-valued bound. By [A3], this is a selected-model energy prediction and not a reported measurement. [A2, A3, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Constructed one-coordinate positive-quartic example on full $L^2$
items.design_state: Complete one-mode verification using the actual full L² model and the quartic energy bound. Its local theorem suppliers are escalated because upstream C01 postulates lack current Step 1 readiness; this item is escalated.
items.statement:
Choose $N=1$, $a=1$, $r=1$, and $\lambda=1$, all dimensionless. The
potential is $V(q)=q^2/2+q^4$, and the physical Hamiltonian is $H_{\rm phys}
=E_*h$ with $E_*>0$ joules. The coordinate-space Hilbert space is the full
$H_1=L^2(\mathbb R,dq;\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]], not a finite matrix truncation.
The positive $q^4$ term is present in the potential of the full form-selected
operator. This is a one-coordinate model; no field-scattering, continuum, or
empirical conclusion is asserted.
items.strategy:
1.1 The parameters satisfy $a>0$, $r>0$, and $\lambda>0$, and $V(q)=q^2/2+q^4\ge q^2/2$, so the coercivity hypotheses hold with $c=1/2$ and $C_0=0$. The coordinate variable $q$ ranges over $\mathbb R$; vectors in $H_1$ are square-integrable complex functions of $q$, identified up to equality almost everywhere by [F3]. The characteristic functions $\mathbf 1_{[3n,3n+1)}$, $n\in\mathbb N$, are nonzero pairwise orthogonal vectors, so this Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. [F3, algebra]

2.1 By [A1], the Countable Choice hypothesis of [F2] holds. Substituting $a=r=\lambda=1$ into it gives $0\le E_g^{\rm phys}(1)-E_g^{\rm phys}(0)\le3E_*/2$. This is an exact bound for the selected model, not an exact value of either ground energy. [A1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [A1], the Countable Choice hypothesis of [F1] holds. Applying [F1]
to the same selected model gives a global unitary group $U_{\rm phys}(\tau)$ for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$, norm preservation for all states, and differentiability precisely on the stated Hamiltonian domain. The quartic coefficient is positive, and the Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional by step 1.1; thus this is a one-coordinate polynomial operator model on the full Hilbert space, not a finite matrix replacement. No observation or continuum extrapolation is asserted. [A1, F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Scope of the Euclidean distribution-extension identity
items.design_state: Complete scope remark based on the current-ready QFT-IR04 proposition and imported choice definition; the claim is ready at this item, without independent approval.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as in
[[prop-qft-four-dimensional-log-scale-anomaly]]. That proposition gives an
exact Euclidean distribution-extension identity for the specified punctured
kernel $u(x)=1/(16\pi^4|x|^4)$: changing its cutoff scale changes the
extension by $(8\pi^2)^{-1}\log(\mu/\nu)\delta_0$. Its statement
explicitly classifies it as a Euclidean distribution identity. By itself it
does not say that an experimentally measured parameter changes with energy
scale, choose which extension a physical model uses, or define a measurement
procedure. It constructs no Lorentzian field theory. This remark asserts
neither existence nor nonexistence of a field theory obtained by taking a
continuum limit and supplies no empirical claim.
items.strategy: Scope remark; no deductive proof claimed.
